counterfactual_missing_items: no mention of classic invasive ductal carcinoma features such as glandular formation or desmoplastic stroma
imaging findings are nonspecific and shared by many cystic-solid breast lesions
decisive_items: dilated ducts with broad papillary structures, a mono- to multilayer epithelial covering, and densely packed tumor cells with moderately atypical nuclei
ER 90%, PR 90%, HER2 negative, Ki-67 20%, CK5/6 negative, E-cadherin positive, p63 negative, calponin negative, and GATA3 positive
absence of myoepithelial markers, lack of a fibrous cystic capsule, and presence of fused papillary networks with abundant fibrovascular cores
response.rationale: R1 relies on diagnostic histopathology and IHC directly from the biopsy, which are definitive and specific. R2 is based only on imaging features (cystic/solid, fluid levels) that are nonspecific and do not exclude other cystic breast neoplasms. The pathology excludes myoepithelial cells and fibrous capsule, favoring an invasive papillary neoplasm over benign cystic lesions; invasive ductal carcinoma is a broad category that fits the aggressive features and IHC profile, while cystic hypersecretory carcinoma is a rare entity not supported by the pathology description.

rejected.why: Imaging-only support is insufficient; the pathology and IHC are the definitive modality and are incompatible with a pure imaging-based diagnosis.
